subject: Residency decision paths: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Residenc y decision paths: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (post-call recap)

Hi Lars / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time earlier — helpful call. Quick written recap so we have the same next steps and to surface a few clarifying questions that will determine whether Hosted, Dedicated, or Private is the right fit for Inkraft.

Recap of requirements we heard on the call:
- Data residency: primary requirement is EU-only storage for customer data and logs. Secondary need: sub-second latency for EU users, but a subset (~15%) of traffic originates from APAC and needs reasonable latency.
- Compliance: SOC2 + possibility of a customer audit within 6 months.
- Traffic profile: expected bursty traffic tied to product events; monthly token estimate ballpark shared on call: ~120M tokens/month.
- Security: KMS integration for keys and strict egress rules for VPC option are important.

What this means in practice:
- Hosted API (EU region): can host inference and store logs in an EU region; fastest time-to-value and simplest rollout. Good if EU residency + no need for on-prem hardware. Cross-region routing to APAC will reduce latency for APAC users but by default the control plane stays with Redwood and traffic may cross region boundaries unless you request strict EU-only egress.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved) in EU: reserved GPU pools deployed into the EU region. Gives predictable throughput, stronger isolation, and we can apply stronger routing policies (e.g., force EU data residency for model storage). Still a managed Redwood control plane, but compute and storage can be region-isolated.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): for customers that require customer-managed networking, HSM-backed KMS, and air-gapped options. Best for customers needing maximum control and auditability, longer lead times and higher ops overhead.

Open questions (please reply inline):
1) Can you confirm the split of traffic EU vs APAC (approx %)?
2) Any hard requirement that cross-region network hops are forbidden (i.e., EU-only egress for all model requests)?
3) Do you have a preferred timeline for pilot vs production (weeks/months)?

Next steps we propose:
- Please complete the short residency questionnaire (link below) so we can build a region-tailored quote and lead-time estimate.
- Technical deep dive with Vivek (SE) to scope Dedicated/Private network architecture — can you share availability for next week?
- I will prepare a comparison matrix (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and an initial quote for EU Dedicated capacity as a reference.

Attachments (stubs): redwood-deployment-matrix.csv, redwood-data-paths-eu-apac.pdf

Thanks — appreciate the discussion.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0142

Onward: I will follow up once Vivek confirms his availability for the technical deep dive.

Subject: Re: Residenc y decision paths: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (post-call recap)

Thanks Marissa — useful summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- Traffic split: approx 85% EU, 15% APAC (APAC users are primarily in Singapore and Sydney).
- Hard residency: EU-only egress for all customer personal data is preferred; we have a handful of enterprise customers that will require proof that logs and model context do not leave the EU.
- Latency: 95th percentile sub-200ms for EU users is ideal; APAC can accept higher latency but we want to avoid >500ms for real-time features.
- Timeline: Pilot in June, production by Q3 if everything looks good.

A few specific technical questions we didn't get to: 
1) If we go Hosted in the EU region, can you guarantee that cached KV/feature stores and logs remain in-region and are not replicated to US regions by default?
2) For Dedicated, is it possible to provision capacity in eu-west (Ireland) and ap-southeast (Singapore) under a single contract so traffic from APAC is served locally?
3) What is lead time for Private (VPC) deployment and is there an option for HSM-backed KMS?

Happy to hop on a follow-up call next week. Vivek — can you confirm whether Hosted can be configured to meet the EU-only egress constraint?

— Lars
Principal Architect, Inkraft
lars@inkraft.io

Hi Lars / Priya — thanks for the quick reply and the traffic breakdown. Answers inline below and proposed timing: 

1) Hosted EU-only egress and in-region storage: 
- Hosted API supports region-specific data residency. For EU region deployments we can configure retention and storage to remain in eu-west-1 (Ireland) or eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) depending on your preference. Logs and short-term KV cache can be restricted to the region; we will provide the residency attestation and SOC2 artifacts. Note: by default the Redwood control plane remains global, but data egress can be limited by policy.

2) Dedicated multi-region contract: 
- We can provision Dedicated pools in multiple regions under a single commercial agreement. That lets you serve APAC traffic from a Singapore pool while keeping EU data residency for EU customers. There are additional costs for cross-region dedicated pools and a minimum commit for each region.

3) Private (VPC) lead time & HSM: 
- Typical lead time for VPC/private installs is 8–12 weeks for initial rollout (depends on hardware shipping and network integration). HSM-backed KMS is supported for Private deployments; it is also possible for Dedicated with an approved exception and enterprise add-on.

Next steps:
- Vivek, can we pick a 60–90 minute tech deep-dive slot next week to map a sample call flow and confirm where KV caches and audit logs will live?
- Lars / Priya, please fill the residency questionnaire (link below) to unlock an accurate quote — I included an initial deployment matrix as an attachment.

I'll prepare a short decision matrix (cost vs time-to-market vs compliance risk) and a rough Dedicated quote to share before the call.

Attachments (stubs): redwood-deployment-matrix.csv, redwood-data-paths-eu-apac.pdf

Best,
Marissa
